newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES - JUNE 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES - JUNE 16.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency signed a preliminary agreement with Belgium's Union Miniere SA for the sale of 56 percent of the MDK copper smelter for $80 million.
The buyer has also to invest $220 million in the Pirdop MDK, which would make the deal Bulgaria's biggest sell-off so far.
-- The new Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) seven-member board takes office this week to head the bank under a currency board system from July 1.

Last week the parliament elected Svetoslav Gavriiski as a BNB governor and Martin Zaimov, Valentin Tsvetanov and Emilia Milanova as deputy governors. The president appointed the remaining three board members.
-- The government approved the 1997 budget draft and is expected to submit it to parliament this week.

A deficit of 5.81 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is assumed in the central government budget and a deficit of 6.16 percent is projected in the broader consolidated state budget, which also includes the budgets of the judicial system, the ministries and the municipalities.
GDP is assumed at 16,150 billion levs, down a real 7.4 percent from 1996.

-- Amoco Corp said it has sold its retail petrol stations in Bulgaria to the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, after announcing last October that it would end its petroleum retailing businesses in eastern Europe as a part of its global policy.
Apart from petrol stations in the cities of Bourgas and Plovdiv, Amoco had two sites in Sofia and another one in the Danube port of Rousse. Shell has built up 23 petrol stations in Bulgaria so far.
-- Belgium's Solvay raised its stake in Bulgaria's biggest soda ash producer Sodi to 66.7 percent from 60 percent on Friday under a share capital rise to 6.283 billion levs from 5.236 billion levs.

-- Prince Kiril, son of Bulgaria's exiled King Simeon II visited Sofia last week to advise President Petar Stoyanov on the speeding up privatisation and development of the local stock market. Prince Kiril is a member of the President's Economic Development Council. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
